breakdown.description: The prompt sets the free-end rotation to zero, even though a cantilever’s free end is generally free to rotate under an end point load.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification correctly allows the free end to rotate, applying boundary conditions only at the fixed end (slope = 0 and deflection = 0 at x = 0). It explicitly computes the free-end slope using theta = PL^2/(2EI), which is non-zero, directly contradicting the flawed instruction that set the free-end rotation to zero.

breakdown.description: The prompt treats the bending moment as constant and equal to P L over the entire span, even though the cantilever moment varies linearly from the free end to the fixed end.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification explicitly states 'Use the linearly varying bending moment M(x) = P(L − x) over the full span,' correctly replacing the flawed constant moment P·L assumption with the proper linearly varying moment distribution for a cantilever under an end point load.
